thread.title: Apple: Investors Cheer Ahead of Updated iPhone Lineup

author: David Marino-Nachison
title: Apple: Investors Cheer Ahead of Updated iPhone Lineup
text:
Photo: Eleven X By David Marino-Nachison Aug. 1, 2018 10:03 a.m. ET If it seems like only yesterday that Apple (AAPL) watchers were waiting impatiently to see whether the tech giant was going to prop up the stock market or bring it crashing down—it was. On Wednesday morning, many investors have decided to it’s OK to breathe again.
Newsletter Sign-up
After the market’s close, the Barron’s Next 50 company turned in fiscal Q3 financial results that met Wall Street’s expectations and a Q4 outlook that exceeded them. (Barron’s Jonathan Swartz wrote our first take .) That was enough to help the stock to a roughly 4% Wednesday morning gain, putting the shares up some 15% for 2018 as they hit new highs for the year.
On Wednesday, Monness Crespi Hardt—already among the Street’s most-bullish Apple analysts—boosted its price target to $275, the highest out there, citing a valuation it says represents a better deal than the S&P 500.
“Apple has delivered a 14% GAAP EPS compounded annual growth rate vs. just 5% for the S&P 500 over the past four years,” wrote analyst Brian White. “However, the S&P 500 index trades at 2019 P/E of nearly 16x and Apple trades at just 12.3x (ex-cash; or 14x straight).”
Investors liked several things about Apple’s quarterly results— including services growth but also an iPhone sales mix that showed increasing average prices that could been encouraging heading into a product line refresh expected later this year.
Illustration: Guggenheim “We continue to expect iPhones to refresh on-time in late September, headlined by much larger screen sizes via both a 6.5” iPhone X Plus. and 6.1” LCD-based iPhone that adds the X’s ‘notch’ for 3-D sensing/Face ID, priced from $749,” wrote Guggenheim.
Average iPhone selling prices should be “relatively stable” in fiscal 2018, PiperJaffray wrote.
And Morgan Stanley thinks services are growing sufficiently that they can help the company grow even if iPhone sales disappoint .
“We see more upside than downside risk to the upcoming iPhone product cycle and a building services narrative,” wrote analyst Katy Huberty. “Even if device revenue growth slows, services and wearables can pick up the slack, delivering 5% revenue and 14% EPS growth annually through 2020.”
Illustration: PiperJaffray Somewhat arbitrary milestone that it is, a market capitalization of $1 trillion seems increasingly inevitable for Apple.
More About Barron’s Next Learn more about Barron’s Next The Barron’s Next 50 “Apple’s strong software capabilities, expanding services business and unique digital ecosystem at large will increasingly be appreciated by investors, driving Apple toward the $1 trillion market cap milestone,” wrote Monness Crespi Hardt’s White. “Apple remains one of the most underappreciated stocks in the world with a valuation that remains depressed.”
